summary.title: Writing a Linux Debugger Part 5: Source and Signals
summary.one_liner: You learn how to use DWARF line tables and function DIEs from a libelfin-based C++ debugger to map a program counter to source lines, print source context at a breakpoint, and decode SIGTRAP causes with PTRACE_GETSIGINFO.
takeaways: Parse the ELF file and its DWARF sections with libelfin, opening the file with a descriptor so it can be mmapped.
Find the function DIE (DW_TAG_subprogram) and line table entry that contain a given program counter by walking compilation units.
For PIE binaries, compute the load address from /proc/<pid>/maps and subtract it from the PC before querying DWARF.
Use PTRACE_GETSIGINFO and si_code (SI_KERNEL, TRAP_BRKPT, TRAP_TRACE) to tell why a SIGTRAP occurred, then print source lines around the current location.
summary.summary: This is part 5 of a series on writing a Linux debugger in C++ using ptrace and libelfin for DWARF parsing. It adds ELF and DWARF loading to the debugger, implements helper functions to find a function DIE and line table entry from a PC, and computes a load address for position-independent executables. It then adds a print_source function that shows a window of source lines with a cursor on the current line. Finally it improves signal handling by using PTRACE_GETSIGINFO to distinguish breakpoint hits from single-step completions. The page is a series entry with a link to a book version.
